concurrent_development_incident.what_happened: While this campaign was in progress, a separate concurrent implementing session pushed 3 more commits to origin/master (8bc9cbb, 2a4ac04, c6b78a9, real timestamps 09:46-09:54 UTC, fixing Bugs 7/9/13/14 from the same #33 thread) and their CI auto-deployed sem-ai-command. This verifier's own first deploy (version 80, 09:58:09 UTC) was pushed from a LOCAL copy based on stale 15e868a HEAD (fetched/rebased AFTER, not before, that deploy) - which briefly overwrote their live deployment with a version missing the Bug 7/9/13/14 fixes.
concurrent_development_incident.real_impact: Checked directly: zero real work_orders rows exist in the 09:58:09-10:19:44 UTC gap window - no real founder traffic was degraded by this.
concurrent_development_incident.resolution: Rebased this verifier's commit onto origin/master (git rebase, 2 real conflicts in qa/KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES.md and the shared pack/errors lines in index.ts, both manually merged to preserve BOTH sets of changes), re-ran all 3 regression scripts + the SQL regression against the merged file (all pass), redeployed (version 81, 10:19:44 UTC) with the fully merged code, then pushed the merged commit (aef616c) to master.
concurrent_development_incident.lesson: Always `git fetch && git rebase origin/master` (or at minimum `git log origin/master` to check for drift) immediately before any `supabase functions deploy` when working in a worktree/session that started from an older commit - a deploy is a real production action independent of git state, and can silently clobber concurrent work that already shipped.
